paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Jesus reads Isaiah's words about good news for the poor, liberty for the captives, and recovery of sight for the blind, and then He says, "Today this Scripture is fulfilled in your hearing." (Luke 4:18, 21) That's not a nice reading. That's Jesus saying the One those words promised is standing right in front of them. The good news has a face, and the face is His.

Now watch what happens with the hometown crowd. They speak well of Him and marvel at His gracious words, but then Jesus tells them about a widow in Sidon and Naaman the Syrian, and everybody in the synagogue is enraged. (Luke 4:22, 25-28) I think this is the hard part, friend: they loved the words until the words said something they didn't want to hear. Liking the Bible when it pats me on the back is easy. Hearing it when it stretches me, THAT takes a humble heart.

So here's what I'm taking to the bakery today. Jesus came to bring good news, and He won't be talked out of it, not by a crowd, not even by a cliff, because "Jesus passed through the crowd and went on His way." Wait, I need to check that one against the page. The text says, "But Jesus passed through the crowd and went on His way." (Luke 4:30) Nothing could stop what He was sent to do. Let Him say the hard thing to you, baker, and stay in the room to hear it, because the good news is worth it.
